title: Building a Professional Resume That Gets Read
excerpt: A practical guide to creating a clear and focused resume that communicates your value without unnecessary complexity.

blocks.text: A strong resume is not a complete history of everything you have ever done. It is a focused document designed for a specific opportunity.
Before writing, study the job description and identify the skills, responsibilities and outcomes that appear repeatedly.
Instead of listing routine responsibilities, describe what changed because of your work.

items: Begin each bullet with a clear action.
Explain the measurable result when possible.
Remove details that do not support the target role.

blocks.text: A resume should make your relevance obvious within the first few seconds.
Use consistent headings, short bullet points and enough whitespace. Recruiters should be able to locate your experience, education and technical skills without searching through dense paragraphs.
Remove vague phrases such as “hard-working” or “responsible for.” Replace them with specific evidence that demonstrates your contribution.
